# webscour

> `webscour` (`wsc`) is a Linux-first, dependency-free Python CLI that fetches the web for agents:
> keyless search through a local SearXNG, page text and markdown, PDF reading, sitemap mapping and
> a polite short crawl. No key. No account. No log.

Everything an agent needs is on this page. The full documentation is one link away at the end.

## What it does

- `wsc search "<query>"` asks a local SearXNG first, falls back to scrapers, and prints numbered
  rows with the engines that produced each one.
- `wsc fetch <url>` turns one page into reading text or markdown, with an optional regex filter.
- `wsc pdf <url|path>` reads a paper or a manual through pdftotext, pandoc or markitdown.
- `wsc map <url>` lists a site's URLs from sitemap.xml, robots.txt or llms.txt.
- `wsc crawl <url>` follows same-origin links for a few pages, one per second.
- `wsc doctor` reports one verdict line for the whole install and exits 1 when it is not `OK`.
- `wsc setup` installs the bundled SearXNG as a systemd user unit on 127.0.0.1:8888.
- `wsc probe` measures which upstream engines your IP can actually use.
- `wsc cache list|get|prune|path` reads the on-disk cache under `./.webscour/`.

## Install

```bash
pipx install webscour                  # recommended
uv tool install webscour
pip install --user webscour
uvx webscour search "sqlite wal mode"  # no install at all
wsc setup                              # the local SearXNG and the lightpanda check
```

Python 3.11 or newer, Linux, and lightpanda on `PATH` for rendering. No Python dependencies exist
by design.

## Sources

`--source web` (default) is the local meta-search. `github`, `so`, `hn`, `arxiv` and
`discourse:<base>` are direct service APIs. Fourteen more are keyless single-purpose endpoints:
`wikipedia`, `openalex`, `crossref`, `arxiv-api`, `europepmc`, `pubmed`, `pypi`, `npm`, `crates`,
`devto`, `wayback`, `googlenews`, `bbc`. None needs a key. `--fresh` restricts the answer to dated
news rows.

## Rules the tool keeps

- stdout is the answer; stderr carries failures and three facts about an answer: `render: <engine>`,
  `route: <name>`, `cache: hit (<age>)`.
- `-v` explains every choice. Without it, a clean run is silent.
- At most one live web query per second, across processes, so a shell loop cannot look like a
  scraper.
- Exit codes: `0` success, `1` a failed verdict or gate, `2` a usage error or a backend that could
  not answer.

## Interfaces

- CLI: `wsc <verb>`, documented above.
- MCP server: `wsc mcp`, a stdio JSON-RPC server exposing one tool, `web_scour`.
- pi extension: `extensions/pi/`, which shells out to `wsc tool-argv` and runs the command it gets
  back.
- `wsc tool-argv --json '<params>'` prints the command line both front ends build, so the mapping
  is inspectable.
